title: LORD, TEACH ME HUMILITY IN SUCCESS AND FAITH IN HARDSHIP
text: Glory to God. Glory to God. Glory to God. We welcome the Holy Spirit into this place. We welcome the presence of the most high God. Father, we thank you for this morning. We thank you for the breath in our lungs. We thank you because you are a God who does not sleep. You do not slumber. And this morning you have preserved us. You have kept us and you have brought us into this sacred moment. Holy Spirit, we yield to you. We yield to your leading, to your teaching, to your conviction, to your power. Have your way in this gathering. Let every heart be open. Let every spirit receive. Let every stronghold fall in the name of Jesus. Father, I thank you for every soul that has gathered here this morning, whether you're watching from wherever you are in the world, whether this is the first time you're tuning in, whether this is a word that has found you at the exact moment you needed it. I want you to know that God is not surprised by where you are. He is not caught off guard by your situation. He knew before the foundations of the earth that this morning you would need this word and he prepared it for you before time [music] began. Hallelujah. The title the Lord gave me, the burden he placed upon my spirit for this hour, is this times, Lord, teach me humility in success and faith in hardship. And I want you to receive this not just as a sermon, not just as a morning message, but as a prayer, as a prophetic assignment, as a repositioning word that will recalibrate your soul for the season that God is taking you into. Write this down somewhere. Say it out loud. Lord, teach me humility in success and faith in hardship. Because, beloved, these are the two mountains that swallow destinies. Success without humility is a trap. Hardship without faith is a grave. And many great men, many anointed women, many people with genuine assignments from God have been buried not by their enemies, not by the devil, but by their inability to carry success with grace, and their inability to carry suffering with trust. Let me open the word of God. Come with me to the book of Deuteronomy chapter 8, verses 10 through 14. The Bible says, "When you have eaten and are satisfied, praise the Lord your God for the good land he has given you. Be careful that you do not forget the Lord your God, failing to observe his commands, his laws, and his decrees that I am giving you this day. Otherwise, when you eat and are satisfied, when you build fine houses and settle down, and when your herds and flocks grow large, and your silver and gold increase, and all you have is multiplied, then your heart will become proud, and you will forget the Lord your God, who brought you out of Egypt, out of the land of slavery. Do not rush past that. Let it land. Moses, one of the most seasoned prophets to ever walk the earth, a man who saw the back parts of God, a man whose face is shown with the glory of the Almighty, this man, at the end of his life, at the end of 40 years of leading a stiff-necked people, what was the final warning? What was the word he left with Israel at the border of their breakthrough? He did not say, "Be careful of your enemies on the other side." He did not say, "Be careful of the giants in the land." He said, "Be careful of yourself when the blessing comes. Be careful of your own heart when God gives you what you have been asking for." This is profound because we spend so much time praying times, "Lord, give me. Lord, open the door. Lord, let the promotion come. Lord, let the business succeed. Lord, let the marriage be restored." Lord, let the children come times, and these are not wrong prayers. These are legitimate, biblical, spirit-filled prayers. But God, in his mercy, is saying, "If I give you all of that, and your heart is not ready to receive it with humility, the blessing becomes the weapon the enemy uses against your soul. You become the danger to your own destiny. Let me tell you something about success. Success is a test. It is arguably the most sophisticated test God ever administers because it does not feel like a test. Suffering feels like a test. When you are going through hardship, you know you are being examined. You know your faith is on trial. >> [music] >> You cry out, you fast, you pray, you hold on. But when the blessing comes, when the doors open, when your name begins to be called, when the resources begin to flow, the test does not announce itself. It is subtle, it is quiet. And before you know it, something has shifted in your heart and you do not even notice when God left the room. King Saul is one of the most heartbreaking stories in all of scripture. Here is a man who started with genuine humility. When Samuel called him, he said, "Am I not a Benjaminite, from the smallest tribe of Israel, and is not my clan the least of all the clans of the tribe of Benjamin? Why do you say such things to me?" He was hiding among the baggage when they tried to crown him king. Hiding among the baggage. He was not campaigning for position. He was not posting on social media about his anointing. He was genuinely humble before God and God said, "This is the man." And the spirit of God came upon him mightily and he prophesied among the prophets and a new heart was given to him. But then success came. Victories came. The armies defeated, the people cheered, the women sang in the streets saying, "Saul has slain his thousands." And something crept into that man's heart. Something quiet, something subtle, something that goes by many names, but at its root, it is simply this. He began to believe that the anointing was his, that the victories were his, that the position belonged to him by right. And the first time God tested that heart, Saul chose his own wisdom over divine instruction. He offered the sacrifice himself, he kept the spoils. God said destroy. He began to edit the commandments of God through the lens of his own reasoning. And God said to Samuel, I regret that I made Saul king because he has turned away from me and has not carried out my instructions. Beloved, that is one of the most terrifying sentences in all of scripture. I regret that I made him king. Not I regret that the enemy attacked him, not I regret that he faced difficulties. I regret that I elevated him because elevation without humility is a setup for divine regret. Now, let me talk to someone here this morning. You are on the verge of something great. God has been preparing a season of extraordinary favor for your life. Doors are about to open that you have wept before for years. Relationships are about to be restored. Businesses are about to take off. [music] Ministries are about to expand. Names are about to be called. And God is sending this word ahead of the blessing because he loves you too much to give you the promotion without also giving you the character to carry it. Humility is not weakness. Please hear me. Humility is not the absence of confidence. Humility is not poverty of mind. Humility is not the inability to recognize your gifts. True biblical humility is an accurate understanding of who you are in relation to who God is. It is the posture that says, "Everything I have was given to me. Everything I carry was placed in me. Every door that opened was opened by a hand greater than mine. And therefore, I have no ground on which to stand and be proud before God or to demean any man who has not yet arrived at where I am." That is humility. Not the false performative loneliness that people put on in church and abandon in boardrooms. Not the kind that says, "I am nothing. I am nothing." while secretly feeling superior. No. The deep, settled spirit-worked conviction that God is the source of all that you are and all that you have. The Apostle Paul understood this. This is a man who by any human reckoning had every reason to boast. >> [music] >> He was educated under Gamaliel, the greatest rabbi of his generation. He had more revelations than most men in scripture. He was caught up to the third heaven. He saw things that human language had no words to express. He planted churches across the known world. He wrote letters that have shaped civilization. And yet he writes in Philippians 4:11, "I have learned in whatsoever state I am, therewith to be content." Notice he says, "I have learned." Contentment and humility are not natural states for the human soul. They are learned. They are cultivated. They are worked into you through seasons, through encounters with the living God, through moments of confronting your own frailty. Paul also writes in 1 Corinthians 15:10, "But by the grace of God I am what I am, and his grace to me was not without effect. [music] I am what I am." He's not denying his gifts. He is not pretending he has no anointing, but the anchor is, "It is by [music] grace." Not by my intelligence, not by my discipline alone, not by my connections, by grace. And that word grace keeps a man humble because grace cannot be earned, and grace cannot be hoarded, and grace can be withdrawn at any time. The moment you forget that your assignment is grace-sustained, [music] you begin to carry yourself in a way that is an offense to the God who gave it. Now, let me turn to the second mountain. Hardship without faith. Come with me to Job chapter 13:15. And I want you to sit with this. "Though he slay me, yet will I trust in him." Stop. Let that breath of scripture fill your lungs this morning. [music] Though he slay me, not though things are little difficult, not though the road is slightly inconvenient, though he, the very God I serve, appears to be the author of my suffering, appears to be the one who has removed his protective hand, appears to be the one who has allowed everything I built to be dismantled times, yet will I [music] trust in him. This is the language of a man who had discovered a dimension of faith that goes beyond prosperity theology, that goes beyond the simple transaction of obedience and blessing. This is the faith that says, "I do not serve God for what he gives me. I serve God for who he is." And who he is does not change based on what I am going through. His character is not contingent upon my circumstances. His faithfulness is not determined by my comfort. He was good before he gave me anything. He was faithful before the testimony. He was worthy of praise before the breakthrough. And if the breakthrough never comes in the timing [music] I expect, he is still God. Beloved, I want to address some people here this morning who are in a season of profound difficulty. You have been faithful, you have been praying, you have been giving, you have been serving, and yet the situation has not changed. The report is still bad, the door is still closed, the relationship is still broken, the body is still sick, the account is still empty. And the enemy has been whispering in your ear, "Where is your God? Did he forget you? Did he lie to you? Was the promise real, or was it just your emotions?" Let me tell you what the enemy does not want you to know. The hardship you are in is not evidence of God's absence. It is often the very context [music] in which God is doing his deepest work. The furnace does not destroy you, it purifies you. The wilderness does not abandon you, it prepares you. The valley of the shadow of death is not the absence of the shepherd. David said, "Even there, thou art with me." Even in the valley, even in the shadow, even in the place that looks like death, you are with me. Jesus learned obedience through suffering. That is what the book of Hebrews says. Although he was a son, he learned obedience through what he suffered. If the son of God in his incarnation had to learn certain dimensions of his assignment through suffering, who are you and I to demand a path that bypasses the furnace? The furnace is not a sign of God's rejection. The furnace is the very place where the fourth man shows up. Three men went in, three men but four came out. The fire did not destroy them. The fire destroyed only what was never supposed to survive the journey. Let me prophesy to someone here. What you are going through right now is burning away the things [music] that would have sabotaged your destiny if they had made it to the other side with you. The fear that was in you, the self-sufficiency that was in you, the idolatry of human approval that was in you, the dependence on your own wisdom that was in you, the fire is targeting [music] what needs to go so that when you emerge, you emerge pure, you emerge powerful, [music] you emerge with a testimony that cannot be argued with and an anointing that does not need human validation. But here is the key. You must have faith in the hardship. You cannot panic in the furnace. You cannot make irrational decisions in the fire. You cannot abandon your assignment just because the journey got difficult. [music] Faith in hardship is not passive resignation. It is not gritting your teeth and surviving. True faith in hardship is an active, aggressive, [music] spirit-energized trust that says, "I know whom I have believed, and I am persuaded that he is able to keep that which I have committed unto him against that day." Second Timothy 1:12. I know, not I hope, not I feel like. I know. Faith has knowledge at its root. It is built on revelation of who [music] God is. And when you know who God is, when you have encountered him, not just conceptually, but in the deep places of your spirit, the hardship does not shake you the way it shakes those who do not know him. I think about Joseph. Here is a man whose life is one of the most dramatic demonstrations of both these mountains in all of scripture. He started with a dream, a genuine God-given dream. And then he was thrown into a pit by his own brothers, sold as a slave, taken to a foreign country, falsely accused, thrown into prison, forgotten, delayed. And at every stage of that impossible journey, the Bible uses one simple phrase to describe his condition, and the Lord was with Joseph. In the pit, the Lord was with Joseph. In Potiphar's house, the Lord was with Joseph. In the prison, the Lord was with Joseph. The geography changed, the circumstances changed. The pain changed, but one constant, the presence of God. And Joseph kept faith in every season. He did not become bitter. He did not become resentful. He did not curse God in the darkness. He served faithfully wherever he was placed. He exercised his gifts even in prison. He remained trustworthy even when it seemed there was nothing to gain from trustworthiness. And then God turned it, and he turned it suddenly. One day Joseph was in prison, and within 24 hours he was dressed in fine linen, with a gold chain around his neck, riding in the second chariot of Pharaoh, with people bowing before him as he rode through the streets [music] of Egypt. That is how fast God can move. That is how suddenly a season can change when it is time. You do not need to know the timeline. You do not need to understand every detour. You do not need to be able to explain the wilderness to the people watching your life. You just need to keep faith in the hardship. And notice when Joseph finally came into his success, [music] he did not forget God. When his brothers came before him, when the moment arrived where he could have exacted revenge, where he could have said, "Look at me now. Where is your pit? Where is your conspiracy? Look how God has elevated me." He wept. He wept. He said, "Do not be grieved or angry with yourselves for selling me here because God sent me ahead of you to preserve life. You meant it for evil, but God meant it for good." That is a man who carried success with humility. That is a man who saw his elevation not as personal vindication, but as divine assignment. That is a man who, even at the height of his power, pointed to God as the author of the story. Lord, teach us to be Josephs. Lord, teach us to have faith in the pit and humility in the palace. Lord, teach us that whether the road is ascending or descending, you are the constant and you are enough. Now, I want to speak to the spiritual architecture of [music] what I'm teaching this morning because this is important. Proverbs 16:18 says, "Pride goes before destruction and a haughty spirit before a fall." This is not a mere proverb. This is a spiritual law. It operates like gravity. You do not suspend it by being sincere. You do not override it by having good intentions. When pride enters a man's heart, destruction is not a possibility, it is a certainty. It is only a matter of time, and God, in his mercy, sometimes allows a man to experience hardship before the elevation, precisely to work humility into him that would not come any other way. The wilderness is often God's classroom. The difficulty is often God's curriculum. The delay is often God's preparation. Moses spent 40 years in the wilderness as a shepherd before God sent him back to Egypt. 40 years. He had been raised in Pharaoh's palace, educated in all the wisdom of Egypt, trained in the arts of war and leadership. By human estimation, he was ready at 40. God said, "No, another 40 years." And what happened in those 40 years in the wilderness? The pride of palace living was stripped away. The self-confidence of Egyptian education was recalibrated. The man who had killed an Egyptian in his own zeal and wisdom discovered that God's work cannot be done in man's flesh. And when he emerged from that wilderness at 80 years old, the Bible describes him as the most humble man on the face of the earth. Not the most educated, not the most charismatic, the most humble. And it was from that posture of humility that he stood before God in a burning bush and received one of the greatest commissions in human history. Beloved, do not despise your wilderness. Do not rush your preparation. Do not be in such a hurry to get to the palace that you bypass the process that makes you fit to rule. God is not slow. God is thorough. And he would rather delay your elevation than have your elevation destroy you. There is a prayer that I want to teach you to pray, not once, not as a formula, but as a posture of the heart. It is the prayer in our title, "Lord, teach me humility in success." Pray it before the success comes. Pray it in anticipation of the blessing. Say, "Lord, I know you are about to do great things in my life. I know the doors are about to open. I know the increase is coming. But Father, more than the blessing, I want the character to carry it. More than the promotion, I want the humility to steward it. Do not let the gifts you give me become walls between [music] me and you. Do not let my success make me a stranger to prayer. Do not let the noise of blessings drown out the voice of the Holy Spirit in my life. Teach me humility in success. And pray these times, Lord, teach me faith in hardship. When the storm comes, and it will come, because Jesus himself said in this world you will have tribulation. When the storm comes, strengthen my faith. Let the roots go deeper when the winds blow harder. Do not let me interpret difficulty as abandonment. Do not let me mistake the silence of God for the absence of God. Do not let a temporary season write a permanent conclusion in my heart. Teach me to stand on your word even when my circumstances contradict it. Teach me to praise you in the dark. Teach me to trust you in the valley. Teach me faith in hardship. This morning I feel the Holy Spirit hovering over some lives. There are people listening to this message who are in two very different places, and yet they need the same word. Some of you are in a season of unprecedented favor. Things are going well. The business is growing. The ministry is expanding. People are calling your name. And this word is a warning and a grace from God to stay [music] low. Stay connected to prayer. Stay accountable to spiritual authority. Stay grateful. Stay generous. Do not let the increase make you inaccessible. Do not let the platform make you proud. Do not let the title make you forget the God who gave you the testimony. And some of you are in the deepest valley of your life. You are reading this message through tears. You are walking through a broken season. The situation looks impossible. The walls feel like they're closing in. And God sent this word to you this morning to say, "Do not let go. Do not quit. Do not make permanent decisions based on temporary pain." The same God who brought Joseph out of prison can bring you out of this. The same God who shut the mouths of lions for Daniel can silence every force that has been assigned against your destiny. The same God who opened the Red Sea when Egypt was behind Israel and the sea was before them, that same God is still in the business [music] of making impossible ways. Hold on, keep faith. The morning is coming. Joy is coming. The testimony is closer than it has ever been. Let me read one more scripture before we go into prayer. Romans 8:28. You have heard it many times, but let it find a fresh place in your heart today. And we know that in all things [music] God works for the good of those who love him, who have been called according to his purpose. In all things, not in some things, not in the pleasant things, not in the things that make sense. In all things, the betrayal God works, the sickness God works, the delay God works, the failure God works, the closed door God works, the broken relationship God works. All things are being orchestrated by a God whose intelligence is infinite, whose love is unconditional, and whose purpose cannot be frustrated. He's working. Even now, he's working. Even in what you cannot see, he's working. Even in what you cannot explain, he's working. And the end result, the Bible guarantees is good, not just okay, good. For those who love him and are called according to his purpose. Now, beloved, I want to encourage you to share this message. Send it to someone who is in a hard season. Send it to someone who just came into a season of blessing and needs this anchor. Send it to a friend who is losing faith. Send it to a brother or sister who needs to be reminded that God is still on the throne. This is a word that needs to travel. This is a prayer that needs to spread because somewhere in your circles, there is a person whose life is about to be transformed by this exact word at this exact moment. You may not know who it is, but God knows. Be obedient. share it, be a carrier of grace this morning. And now let us pray. Let us go before the [music] throne with everything we have. Let the Holy Spirit carry your request before the Father. Let this be a moment of genuine encounter. Pray with me. Father, we come before you this morning with open hands and open hearts. We come not with a performance, not with religious noise, but with genuine hunger. We come with the reality of our lives laid bare before your omniscience. You know everything about us, the struggles we have not told anyone, the fears that visit us in the night, the questions we are afraid to ask, the wounds that have not yet healed, the hopes that we are afraid to hope again. Father, you know. And we come before you not to hide but to yield. Lord, we declare with every breath in our bodies you are God. Not just in theory, not just in doctrine. You are God over our marriages. You are God over our finances. You are God over our health. You are God over our children. You are God over our businesses [music] and our ministries and our nations. You are God and there is no other. And in the light of who you are we bow. We bow in worship. We bow in surrender. We bow in the deep settled conviction that you are worthy of everything we are and everything [music] we have. Now, Holy Spirit, we ask for the gift of humility. We are not too proud to acknowledge that pride has worked its way into corners of our hearts that we have not fully surrendered. There are areas where we have taken for what God did. There are places where we have walked with more confidence in our own abilities than in the grace of God. There are moments where success, small or large, has made us slightly less desperate for you. Father, forgive us. And more than forgiveness, we ask for transformation. Work through humility into our DNA. Work it deep. Work it real. Work it lasting. Let it not be the kind of humility we perform in church but the kind we carry into the boardroom, into the kitchen, into the relationships, into the places where no one is watching. Let it be real. Let it be sustained by the Holy Spirit. Let it be the kind that causes us to be genuinely moved by other people's victories. Genuinely able to serve without recognition. Genuinely content to be the hand that God uses without needing the applause. Father, we pray for every person who is about to receive a promotion that they've been waiting for. God, go ahead of that and prepare their heart. Let the humility come before the honor. Let the character catch up with the gift. Let them not enter their next season with the pride that would poison the blessing. Prepare them, Lord. Make them ready. Not just for the work, but for the weight of the favor. And Father, we pray for faith in hardship. Lord, there are people in this moment who are walking through situations that make no sense. They have done everything right. They have prayed, they have trusted, they have given, they have served, and the situation has not changed. And they are tired, Lord. They are genuinely tired. And the enemy is using that tiredness to whisper doubt into their hearts. Father, this morning, like you did for Elijah under the juniper tree, touch them again. Not with a sermon. Touch them with [music] your actual presence. Let them feel your nearness. Let them know with every fiber of their being that you have not abandoned them. You have not forgotten them. You have not shelved their name. You are with them. You are working. You are moving on their behalf even now. We command doubt to leave. In the name of Jesus, we bind every spirit of discouragement that has settled upon the minds of God's people this [music] morning. Every spirit of hopelessness, we bind you. Every assignment of the enemy that is designed to make God's people give up one step before the breakthrough, we dismantle you by the authority of the risen Christ. We destroy the works of the enemy over these lives. We pull down strongholds of fear. >> [music] >> We pull down the stronghold of unbelief. We pull down the lies that say God does not care, that say the promise was not real, that say you have gone too far or waited too long. Every lie we pull it down by the power of the word of God. Now we declare over this gathering Isaiah 40:31. Those who hope in the Lord will renew their strength. They will soar on wings like eagles. They will run and not grow weary. They will walk and not be faint. We receive this renewal this morning. Strength is being renewed right now. Faith is being rebuilt right now. Hope is being restored right now. Every person who came into this morning's prayer broken in spirit, the Holy Spirit is mending what is broken. He is restoring what the enemy stole. He is renewing what discouragement depleted. Father, we pray for the marriages represented in this gathering. Marriages that are under pressure, marriages that are strained, marriages where communication has broken down, where intimacy has cooled, where the enemy has brought confusion and misunderstanding, Lord, we ask [music] for a supernatural restoration. Let the love of God be poured out in these homes. Let forgiveness flow. Let pride be broken between spouses. Let the humility that we are praying for personal success extend into our relationships. Lord, let couples love each other the way Christ loves the church with patience, with sacrifice, with a love that does not keep records of wrongs. We pray for the children in the lives of this community. Lord, every child who is going through confusion, every young person who is at a crossroads, every young mind that the enemy is targeting with perversion and destruction and wrong company and wrong ideology, Father, we raise a standard against every assignment of the enemy over this generation. We declare that your sons and daughters shall prophesy. [music] We declare that God's purpose will be fulfilled in this generation. We declare that the children of the righteous shall be mighty in the earth. We command every demonic assignment against the children to be broken in the name of Jesus. We pray for the finances of this community. Lord, every financial lack, every business under pressure, every entrepreneur who is about to give up, every person who has sown faithfully and is waiting for harvest. Father, we invoke the principle of Galatians 6:9. In due season, we shall reap if we do not faint. We declare that the season of harvest is arriving. We declare that the blessing of the Lord makes rich and adds no sorrow. We declare unusual favor over businesses, over careers, over investments, over every legitimate [music] work of these hands. Let the windows of heaven be opened. Let the blessings that have been held up in the realm of the spirit be released now. We receive supernatural increase. We receive divine ideas and strategies. We receive connections that God has ordained. We receive everything that belongs to us by covenant. Father, we pray for the sick among us. Every sickness, every disease, [music] every infirmity, we bring it before the throne of grace this morning. The same Jesus who healed all manner of sickness and disease when he walked the earth is alive today and his healing power has not diminished by a single degree. By his stripes, we were healed, past tense. It is already accomplished at Calvary. We receive healing. We receive wholeness. We declare life over everybody that has received a bad medical report. We declare that the same spirit that raised Christ from the dead and dwells in us is quickening our mortal bodies. Be healed in the name of Jesus. Now, Father, we come back to the heart of this prayer. We ask for this one thing above all other things today. Teach us. Be our teacher. Holy Spirit, be the relentless, patient, gracious teacher of our hearts. In the seasons of abundance, teach us to remain anchored in you, to remain generous, to remain humble, to remain in a posture of gratitude. Let our success always [music] be a testimony to your grace and never a monument to our ego. And in the seasons of hardship, teach us to hold fast to your word. Teach us to worship in the storm. Teach us to trust the process. Teach us that the test is not [music] the conclusion. Teach us that the pit is not the destination. Teach us that the prison is not the final chapter. Teach us the faith of Job, the patience of Joseph, the boldness of Daniel, the trust of Abraham, the kind of faith that calls those things that are not as though they are, that staggered not at the promise of God through unbelief, that was fully persuaded that what God had promised, he was also able to perform. We receive this word as seed this morning. We receive it by faith. We declare that it will not return void. We declare that the transformation it carries has already begun in every heart that has engaged with it in sincerity. What God has started this morning, he will complete. He who began a good work will carry it on to completion until the day of Christ Jesus. Father, we trust you with our lives. We trust you with our families. We trust you with our futures. We trust you with the things we do not understand. We trust you with the silence. We trust you with the storm. We trust you in the sunshine. We trust you in every season because you are Lord of all seasons, and your mercy endures forever. Bless every soul that has prayed this prayer this morning. Bless every heart that has received [music] this word. Let it travel. Let it reach the places that need it. Let it be multiplied. Let it produce fruit in strange places and unexpected lives. God get all the glory. Not to us, Lord. Not to us, but to your name be glory for your love and your faithfulness. We seal this prayer in the matchless incomparable all-sufficient name of Jesus Christ, the same yesterday, today, and forever. The lion of the tribe of Judah, the bright and morning star, the author and finisher of our faith, the alpha and the omega, the one who was and is and is to come. In his name we have prayed. In his name we have decreed. In his name we stand in faith. Amen and amen >> [music] >> and amen. God bless you this morning. You are not the same as when you started. Something moved in the realm of the spirit on your behalf today. Carry this word with you. Revisit it. Pray it again. Share it with someone who needs it and go into your day with your head up and your heart surrendered, knowing that the God who holds the universe holds you. Be blessed. Be strengthened. Be filled in Jesus' name.
